name: Async context propagation
pitch: Add request-id propagation through async context for distributed logging across services.
instructions: Start by listing the project root and finding files that import or use logging. When nothing is found, say so and stop. Read each file that defines a logger or wraps async functions. Identify where request IDs are created, usually at the entry point of a request. Insert code that stores the request ID in an async context variable at the start of each request, and read that variable inside log statements. If a file uses a logger from another module, update the logger call to include the context variable. When all files are updated, run the test suite to check that logs now include the request ID across async boundaries. If the test suite fails, say what error appears and stop. When complete, show the changed lines and the new log format.

skills.name: update-logger-calls
skills.description: Find every log call in the codebase. Add the request ID from async context as the first argument. When a log call already has a context object, merge the request ID into it. When a log call uses positional arguments, insert the request ID before the message. Save each file after changing it.
skills.body: 1. Search for 'logger.' or 'log.' in all Python files. 2. For each match, check if an async context variable exists. 3. If not, create a variable that holds the request ID at the start of the async function. 4. Insert that variable as the first argument to the log call. 5. Save the file. 6. Repeat for every log call.

readme:
# Async context propagation
Adds request-id propagation through async context for distributed logging.

- Reads project files and updates logger calls to include the request ID from async context.
- Runs the test suite to verify logs contain the request ID across async boundaries.
- Will not modify production configuration or deploy code.
- Needs the file_read, file_write and shell_run tools.
